title: Electrochemical direct air capture by local alkalinity generation at three-dimensional interfaces
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74879-z

Carbon capture from air using electrochemistry offers a scalable route to removing CO2 from the atmosphere. Here, the authors report a platform employing a three-dimensional reactive interface to achieve high capture rates with competitive energy consumption.

title: Single-cell analyses identify the ginseng embryonic protoderm as a native compartment for high-efficiency ginsenoside production
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74881-5

Liu et al. identify the ginseng embryonic protoderm as a native, ginsenoside-producing compartment through single-cell analysis. They further develop complementary epigenetic and genetic strategies to enhance metabolite output, presenting a scalable and sustainable alternative to conventional field cultivation.

title: Diverse radical transformations of allenic C(sp)–C(sp<sup>2</sup>) and C(sp<sup>3</sup>)–C(sp<sup>2</sup>) bonds enabled by silyl substitution
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74846-8

While the oxidative cleavage of olefins is well established, the radical-mediated, chemo- and regioselective cleavages of allene C(sp)–C(sp2) and C(sp3)– C(sp2) bonds remain unresolved challenges in synthetic chemistry. Herein, the authors present base metal-catalyzed cleavage of allenic C(sp)–C(sp2) double bonds and C(sp3)–C(sp2) single bonds utilizing air as an oxidant.

title: Spatially explicit temperature optima improve climate impact assessment of global crop productivity
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74564-1

Current agricultural climate models often rely on constant optimal temperatures for crops globally, ignoring local adaptation. This study maps spatially explicit temperature optima for four major staple crops, improving predictions of future global productivity.

title: Geometric phase sensing using seismic waves for comprehensive volcano monitoring at Kı̄lauea Hawaii
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73998-x

This study introduces geometric phase sensing, a topological acoustics framework using seismic noise to track volcanic activity at Kīlauea. The method reveals subsurface changes over the full eruptive stages and enables monitoring across diverse dynamic Earth systems.

title: Ligand-controlled sequential activation enables nickel-catalysed alkyl–alkynyl coupling
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74943-8

Cross-electrophile coupling between unactivated alkyl halides and alkynyl halides has long been challenged by reactivity mismatch and poor chemoselectivity. Here the authors report nickel-catalysed crosselectrophile coupling enabled by a tridentate ligand that controls the sequence of electrophile activation, allowing direct construction of alkynyl–alkyl bonds.

title: Ultrafast photoreduction driven by interfacial spin exchange in manganese-doped quantum dots
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74659-9

The authors show that manganese-doped quantum dots enable ultrafast electron transfer and reduce methyl viologen even when conventional band-edge charge transfer is unfavorable, identifying spin exchange as the key driver of hot-carrier photochemistry.

title: A fourth subgenome of the Camelina genus reveals gene dominance is influenced by chromosomal proximity
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74800-8

The Camelina genus comprises diploid, tetraploid, and hexaploid species. Here, the authors complete genome assembly of ploidy series by assembling genomes of a tetraploid and two hexaploid C. microcarpa accessions, along with the cultivated hexaploid C. sativa, and reveal chromosomal proximity–driven gene dominance.
